azimuth_deg.title: Azimuth Deg
azimuth_deg.description: Apparent azimuth of the disc centre (light time + stellar aberration), deg, 0-360, clockwise from north, in the site's topocentric frame (east-north-up at the site, from the normal to the 1737.4 km reference sphere, MOON_ME_DE421); the same frame as the horizon profile (HorizonProfile.azimuth_deg)

elevation_deg.title: Elevation Deg
elevation_deg.description: Apparent elevation of the disc centre (light time + stellar aberration), deg, measured from the local horizontal plane: the plane through the observer (DEM surface + unit height) normal to the reference sphere's radius at the site; the same plane as the horizon profile (HorizonProfile.elevation_deg). Not the elevation above the terrain: see clearance_deg

visible_fraction.title: Visible Fraction
visible_fraction.description: Visible fraction of the disc, 0..1, against the terrain horizon: Sun = share of the disc's light (limb-darkened, 550 nm), Earth = share of its area (methodology section 5.1)

clearance_deg.title: Clearance Deg
clearance_deg.description: Disc centre elevation minus the terrain horizon elevation at its azimuth, deg

BodyTrack.title: BodyTrack
BodyTrack.description: Per-sample values for one body; every list has the length of `SeriesResponse.time`.

earth_visibility_fraction.title: Earth Visibility Fraction
earth_visibility_fraction.description: Fraction of the window with any part of the Earth disc visible

earth_full_disc_fraction.title: Earth Full Disc Fraction
earth_full_disc_fraction.description: Fraction of the window with the whole Earth disc above the terrain horizon

longest_earth_gap_h.title: Longest Earth Gap H
longest_earth_gap_h.description: Longest continuous period with no part of the Earth disc visible, clipped to the window, h

longest_earth_gap_clipped.title: Longest Earth Gap Clipped
longest_earth_gap_clipped.description: True if the longest Earth gap starts before window_start or runs past window_end, so its full length is longer than longest_earth_gap_h; false if it lies inside the window or there is none

earth_elevation_deg.description: Apparent elevation of the Earth's disc centre above the local horizontal plane (not the terrain horizon): min, max and time mean over the whole window, whether or not the Earth is visible, deg

earth_clearance_deg.description: Earth disc centre elevation minus the terrain horizon elevation at its azimuth: min, max and time mean over the whole window, deg

sun_earth_overlap_fraction.title: Sun Earth Overlap Fraction
sun_earth_overlap_fraction.description: Fraction of the window with any part of both the solar and the Earth disc visible

time_to_earthset_h.title: Time To Earthset H
time_to_earthset_h.description: From window_start to the first Earthset (the last part of the Earth disc going below the terrain horizon), h. Null if not computed, or if there is no Earthset in the window (earthset_in_window false)

earthset_in_window.title: Earthset In Window
earthset_in_window.description: True if at least one Earthset occurs in the window, false if none does (time_to_earthset_h is then null). Null only if not computed

CommsMetrics.title: CommsMetrics
CommsMetrics.description:
F4 (direct-to-Earth at the unit height). Nullable: null = not computed. See methodology section 5.

Earth visible = any part of the Earth disc above the terrain horizon; a gap = no part of it above.
Gaps that start before window_start or run past window_end are clipped to the window.

illumination_fraction.title: Illumination Fraction
illumination_fraction.description: Fraction of the window that is sunlit (any part of the solar disc visible)

mean_visible_disk_fraction.title: Mean Visible Disk Fraction
mean_visible_disk_fraction.description: Time average over the window of the visible share of the solar disc's light, weighted by limb darkening at 550 nm (a light-weighted fraction, not a geometric area fraction)

sunlit_duration_h.title: Sunlit Duration H
sunlit_duration_h.description: Total sunlit time in the window (any part of the solar disc visible), h

longest_sunlit_period_h.title: Longest Sunlit Period H
longest_sunlit_period_h.description: Longest continuous sunlit period (any part of the solar disc visible), clipped to the window, h

longest_shadow_h.title: Longest Shadow H
longest_shadow_h.description: Longest continuous shadow period (no part of the solar disc visible), clipped to the window, h

longest_shadow_clipped.title: Longest Shadow Clipped
longest_shadow_clipped.description: True if the longest shadow period starts before window_start or runs past window_end, so its full length is longer than longest_shadow_h; false if it lies inside the window or there is none

shadow_count.title: Shadow Count
shadow_count.description: Number of shadow periods (no part of the solar disc visible) in the window, with no minimum duration; periods clipped to the window count. Partial loss of the disc is not a shadow

sun_elevation_deg.description: Apparent elevation of the Sun's disc centre above the local horizontal plane (not the terrain horizon): min, max and time mean over the whole window, whether or not the Sun is visible, deg

sun_azimuth_deg.description: Apparent azimuth of the Sun's disc centre, deg clockwise from north, over the whole window, whether or not the Sun is visible. min and max are the ends of the smallest arc containing the track, read clockwise from min to max (min > max when the arc crosses north). A full circle is reported as min 0, max 360. mean is always null: an average azimuth has no meaning here

time_to_sunset_h.title: Time To Sunset H
time_to_sunset_h.description: From window_start to the first sunset (the last part of the solar disc going below the terrain horizon), h. Null if not computed, or if there is no sunset in the window (sunset_in_window false)

sunset_in_window.title: Sunset In Window
sunset_in_window.description: True if at least one sunset occurs in the window, false if none does (time_to_sunset_h is then null). Null only if not computed

PowerMetrics.title: PowerMetrics
PowerMetrics.description:
F3. Nullable: null = not computed. Exact definitions: docs/methodology.md section 5.

Sunlit = any part of the solar disc above the terrain horizon; shadow = no part of it above. Sunlit and
shadow periods tile the window. Periods that start before window_start or run past window_end are
clipped to the window and still counted.
